quotes.text: If you have a checkbox your customer must accept that only contains a link, the issuer might reject it as unsatisfactory evidence that your customer was aware of your policies.
This doesn’t prevent you shipping to a different address, though you should do all you can to mitigate the risks involved.

If [your plan](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works.md#compare-plans) supports this feature, you can place certain payments into [review](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/transaction-reviews.md).

If [your plan](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works.md#compare-plans) supports this feature, you can manually capture these payments in the [review process](https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/prevention/best-practices.md#manually-review-payments).

Payments that have been authenticated with 3D Secure might be protected from most fraudulent disputes through a rule known as [liability shift](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/3d-secure/authentication-flow.md#disputed-payments).

old_evidence.text: ## Tools for users of Radar for Fraud Teams
[Radar for Fraud Teams](https://stripe.com/radar/fraud-teams) includes a [review](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/reviews.md) feature that allows you to place certain payments into review
With Radar for Fraud Teams you can manually capture these payments in the [review process](https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/prevention/best-practices.md#manually-review-payments).
You can require your users to agree to your terms of service to increase the likelihood that card issuers respect your policies in the event of a dispute.
the issuer might reject it as unsatisfactory evidence
This doesn’t prevent you shipping to a different address, though you should do all you can to mitigate the risks involved.

findings: The newly captured page broadens the section heading from Radar for Fraud Teams to Radar but explicitly makes manual review and manual capture in the review process conditional on the account plan (new lines 85, 91, 160; old lines 84, 90, 159). The current summary's Radar for Fraud Teams heading and unconditional review-queue instruction at source lines 24-28 should be brought into line with that qualification.

Both captures frame terms-of-service agreement as recommended issuer-evidence practice: a business can require agreement, and an issuer might reject a link-only checkbox; reasonable evidence must show a full copy of the policy was presented before purchase (old lines 18-24; new lines 19-25). The source lines 17 and 43 and disputes concept line 56 overstate this as a universal checkout requirement and certain issuer rejection. Recommend conditional advice and preserve the presentation/evidence distinction.

Both captures call shipping to an AVS-verified billing address safest but expressly allow a different destination with risk mitigation and order review (old lines 66-78; new lines 67-79). The disputes concept line 57 says to ship only to AVS-verified addresses and must be reconciled to this conditional guidance, without implying that an unverified destination proves the recipient is fraudulent.

The new capture retains the distinction that a Radar review normally follows processing and charging unless authorization and capture are separated (new line 91); authorization holds funds without moving money, expires if uncaptured, and only captured payments can be disputed (new lines 156-160). This is a payment-state qualification, not evidence of any actual merchant action.

The diff's other changes are mostly wording, italics, link destinations, heading whitespace, table formatting, and a See also navigation footer. The original anti-fraud recommendations and their caveats largely persist; the footer is navigation, not a new factual source.

Existing source lines 33 and 35 and disputes concept line 58 overstate retained raw guidance: Stripe recommends processing on its platform because it cannot determine CE 3.0 eligibility or submit evidence for externally processed transactions (new lines 122-129), while 3DS-authenticated payments might be protected from most fraudulent disputes and Early Fraud Warnings can still count toward monitoring programs (new lines 144-146). Qualify both source and concept; do not equate processing or authentication with guaranteed eligibility, liability shift, or a win.
substantive_changes: Plan-qualified manual Radar review replaces the prior Radar for Fraud Teams product-specific phrasing, without proving that every Radar plan has the feature.

Plan-qualified manual capture within the review process replaces the prior Radar for Fraud Teams phrasing; ordinary separate authorization and capture guidance is retained. The policy, shipping, CE 3.0, and 3DS corrections are retained-claim reconciliation, not newly introduced rules.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the old capture's anti-fraud context and the new capture's continuing full-policy presentation advice, shipping-proof, conditional refund, delayed shipping, address-verification preference with alternate-shipping risk mitigation, payment-information, alert, and customer-friction guidance rather than treating unchanged text as removed.
Keep Radar review's processed-and-charged default distinct from an uncaptured authorization, and keep the new plan eligibility condition visible.
Keep the source's 2026-05-10 historical raw reference and add the 2026-11-07 capture as a separate dated raw source only if the coordinator approves a canonical update.
conflicts: Current source lines 24-28 label manual review as a Radar for Fraud Teams tier, while new raw lines 85 and 91 label the tier Radar and condition the review feature on plan support.

Current source lines 17 and 43 and disputes concept line 56 turn optional agreement advice and possible issuer rejection of a link-only checkbox into universal requirements; both old raw lines 18-24 and new raw lines 19-25 are conditional.
Disputes concept line 57 says to ship only to AVS-verified addresses, whereas both old raw lines 66-78 and new raw lines 67-79 allow a different address with appropriate mitigation and review.

Disputes concept lines 56-58 retain a stale Radar Fraud Teams tier without the new plan condition and imply Stripe processing establishes CE 3.0 eligibility and 3DS establishes liability shift; new raw lines 85-93, 122-129, 144-146, and 160 require qualifications.
Current source line 37 says to use auth and capture with the Radar review queue without the new raw line 160 plan-supported manual-capture condition.
Current source lines 33 and 35 use stronger CE 3.0 eligibility and 3D Secure liability-shift wording than either captured raw page supports; the same issue is present in disputes concept line 58.
unresolved_questions: This capture does not identify which Radar plans support manual reviews or in-review capture; linked plan documentation was outside this exact job and was not fetched.
The page's general seven-day capture wording is unchanged across snapshots; this comparison alone does not establish method-specific authorization windows or current network exceptions.
